title: flshell2 on fresh seeds 6 and 7: the shell makes gliders faster (median 0.69/0.58 vs 0.48 without feedback; up to 17.5 body lengths) and a starved daughter dies on the one valid fork, but division does not replicate: 3 persistent splits and generation 2 on both seeds with the shell, against generation 5 without it
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seeds 6 and 7 (t=800, one planted noise patch) with the shell feedback (h5=0.3) and without it (h5=0, the ablation), plus the claim's dfork.py. With the shell: top-track median speed 0.687/0.575, max 17.5/15.5 body lengths, but 3 and 3 persistent splits with max generation 2 and 2 (merge/split 0.82/0.77; pack/seed6/lineage.png shows many short, fragmenting tracks). Without the feedback: speed 0.481/0.484, max 12.0/12.9 body lengths, 7 and 9 persistent splits, generation 5 and 5. The shell profile replicates (shellprof.json: S peaks at the shell radius, median closure 24/24 sectors, 55% fully closed). Fork seed 6 (t=185, pair 26.7 px): the starved daughter goes 97 -> 0 while its sister grows to 367 and the same daughter in the fed twin ends at 95. Fork seed 7 is invalid: the pair re-merges right after the fork in both arms, so both trackers follow one body.

verdicts.limitation: D is the problem. On both fresh seeds the shell world reaches only generation 2 (3 persistent splits), while the shell-free ablation reaches generation 5, so the shell trades division for speed here, and IBMED is not shown together on these seeds. One valid fork of two. S is a set-point readout of the body with one feedback term, so B is a contour that does work rather than an independent layer.
